design.principle: Earn the acknowledgement by READING, never by assuming.
mechanism: At flush time the store records, beside `pendingFlushIssued`, an `issuedFlush = { campaignId, baseVersion, envelopeDigest }`. It is EVIDENCE, not a claim the write landed - the flush still never reads its response.

On the visible transition `reconcileAfterDiscardFlush` GETs the record through `fetchCampaignRecord`, a one-line extraction of the exact fetch `runLoad` already performs (same `/api/campaigns/[id]` route, same `cache: 'no-store'`). No new route, no second read surface.

It adopts `baseVersion + 1` ONLY when the returned record sits at that revision AND digests to the envelope this client sent. Version alone is refused by design: another device writing at the same moment also lands N+1, and adopting that would hand this client a compare-and-swap token for a record it has never read.

Adoption runs through the existing `applySavedRecord`, then restores `dirty: true`: what is adopted is the TOKEN, not the acknowledgement. The re-armed ordinary save is what earns and clears the pending state.

The read is published as `inFlightLoad`, the primitive whose own docstring states this exact hazard ('a load replaces baseVersion; a save that reads the token while a load is running would send a version the server has already moved past'). The reconciliation also clears the armed timer first, so a mutation's stale-token save cannot race the read - exactly one save follows.
Every failure path (read error, non-2xx, wrong version, digest mismatch) leaves today's behaviour untouched: re-arm, send the old token, let the CAS decide. A 409 there is a REAL conflict.

digest.function: sha256Sync(toCanonicalJson({schemaVersion, campaignId, savedAt, originDeviceId, body})) -- both helpers already in the repo at src/utils/events/hashUtils.ts, no new dependency
digest.excluded: version, instanceId and authority, because prepareCampaignWrite (CampaignPersistenceService.ts:354-407) pins all three on persist -- including them would make a record we ourselves wrote fail its own comparison
digest.whyToCanonicalJsonNotTheJournalCanonical: the comparison spans a real JSON round-trip through the SQLite row, and toCanonicalJson models exactly that (key-sorted JSON.stringify, so an undefined-valued key is absent on both sides). canonicalizeJsonV1 is strict JCS and FAILS on `undefined`, which would throw on the discard path.
digest.whySavedAtCarries: it is minted per envelope build (campaignEnvelope.ts:44), so the digest identifies THIS write rather than merely a state that looks like ours
digest.costMeasured: 1.5-2.1 ms for a 32 KB envelope (node 22, js-sha256 + the same replacer), measured this session -- not a material cost on a discard path

specCitations: openspec/changes/design-campaign-authority-and-sync/specs/campaign-authority/spec.md:178-182 -- 'A hidden transition the document survives still reaches an acknowledged save': the client SHALL schedule an ordinary ACKNOWLEDGED save and SHALL NOT be left holding pending mutations with no write scheduled. Before this fix only the scheduling half held; the save was refused.

same file, 'An unread flush never claims a revision it did not earn': the client SHALL NOT have recorded the flush's revision as acknowledged. Honoured - the revision is recorded only after a READ proves the row is ours, and dirty stays true so the flush itself still acknowledges nothing.

same requirement's preamble: 'its response is not read, so the client SHALL NOT advance its cached base version or clear its dirty state on the strength of having fired it.' The base version now advances on the strength of a READ, never of having fired.
design.deviationFromBrief: The brief's prose suggested `applySavedRecord` (which clears `dirty`) in the ordinary case and keeping `dirty` only when `markDirty` ran after the flush. That reading conflicts with the brief's own required row (1) and with the browser expectation it prescribes (a reconciliation PUT at N+1 answering 200). Resolved in favour of the spec text, which demands an ordinary ACKNOWLEDGED save on every surviving-document path: `dirty` is always restored after adoption and the save always fires.

nonClaims: CO-OP IS UNTOUCHED. `isCoopCampaign` still short-circuits both the flush and the reconciliation, before any read is issued. Residual (2), the co-op dual-writer PUT 409 storm, is not addressed and no co-op path was exercised.

NO ROUTE CHANGE. `src/pages/api/campaigns/[id].ts` is not modified, and neither is the strict compare-and-swap in `CampaignPersistenceService.ts:126-131`. The reconciliation GET uses the existing GET handler.

THE FLUSH IS STILL UNREAD. `fireKeepaliveFlush` is byte-identical: no response read, no `applySavedRecord`, no `baseVersion` advance, no retry, no queued follow-up. Only the SURVIVING-document path reads anything, and it reads the record, not the flush's response.
The legacyUnadopted guard, the conflict guard, the at-most-one-per-pending-set flag and the 64 KiB over-cap skip are all unchanged; their rows still pass untouched.
The over-cap skip remains jsdom-only -- no browser case pushes an envelope past 64 KiB.
Task 1.6's checkbox is NOT flipped and no openspec file was edited.
No push, no PR, no merge. The commit sits on codex/roadmap-r2-client-crash-window-browser-20260915 at 877cd2bf8.
Chromium only. The reconciliation is plain fetch and not engine-sensitive, but no Firefox or WebKit run was made.

The digest proves the stored record carries the bytes this client sent at the revision its write would have produced. It is not a cryptographic authentication of authorship: a different writer that sent a byte-identical envelope with the same savedAt millisecond would also match. That case is indistinguishable from ours and harmless -- the state is the same either way.

A campaign whose reconciliation read is slow leaves the ordinary save unscheduled for one round trip. The armed timer is cleared first and re-armed on every path, so no write is lost, but the 'no pending write scheduled' window is a round trip wide rather than zero.
Case (a) is NOT green in this session. Its failure is shown to pre-date the change by direct A/B at the parent commit; no fix and no root cause for it is claimed.
